"Every journey your real users actually took, ranked by how often they take it. This is your starting point: pick a journey that matters, generate its plan, and turn real usage into a test. Journeys never disappear from this list once you've built for them — their lifecycle stays visible from Planned through Passing, with the evidence behind each state. Status describes what the user did; Planned / Tested remain compatibility badges for the local artifacts; ≈ Suite is a best-effort guess that one of your existing hand-written tests may already cover it — a guess, not a guarantee."

"This page shows sessions already stored on your machine. It contacts PostHog when you ask for new data — Check for new sessions, Rebuild from scratch, any plan button, a Suite Health check — and on its own to check that replays are still available, when an auto-check schedule you set runs, and when the stored data does not cover what you are viewing."
"Contacts PostHog. Reads only sessions newer than your stored history — your stored data is kept and extended. Typically fast."
"Contacts PostHog. Clears your locally stored scan history for this project and re-reads everything from PostHog. Slowest option — use when you suspect the stored data is wrong."
"Checks for new sessions on this schedule while this tab is open. Nothing runs when the tab is closed. Your choice is saved on this machine."
"Since this scan: [N] journeys planned, [N] plans removed."
"Show only journeys that reached a known end."

"Show only journeys where someone typed something and then landed on a new page, with no form submit seen. A journey that creates one record can be planned; one that creates several in a row cannot yet."
"Show only journeys where a form was submitted but the outcome wasn't confirmed."

"A rage click or a thrown error the recording caught. We never guess a bug from how far someone got."
"Marking a journey reviewed is remembered on this machine. If the way we recognise this journey changes, the mark clears."
"Max number of ranked journeys to show. In Journey families view, a journey family counts as one top-level row; an expanded family draws its first 25 paths and offers a Show-all that draws the rest."
"Similar paths through the same flow are grouped into journey families."

"Wizards that track progress in the URL (like ?step=2) now appear as a journey family — one row per step reached — instead of a single row with a depth chart. Same data, clearer view of where people stop. Wizards that keep one URL still show the 'How far people got' depth panel."

"Planned: a plan exists. Scaffolded: the test file exists. Executed: we saw it run. Passing: its last run passed and still matches the file."
"Whether a reviewable test plan has been generated for this journey yet. Click the ✓ to open it in Plans."
"Whether a runnable Playwright test has been scaffolded for this journey yet. Click the ✓ to open it in Tests."

"Best-effort match against your existing test suite — heuristic: a spec that visits this journey's entry (first page) and asserts its final URL (last page). NOT a guarantee — a miss can just mean the heuristic couldn't confirm it, not that no test exists. Only shown when replaytest itself hasn't Planned/Tested this journey yet (that exact match always wins)."

"Generate plan contacts PostHog to fetch this completed session's full recording, then writes a local reviewable plan." / "Fetches this session's full recording from PostHog to generate a reviewable plan. This action contacts PostHog."
"Opens the representative session: one real example of this journey, not all of them. The recording may have expired in PostHog, so its replay player may be empty or missing."
"This plan was built before your journey-matching rules changed, so its coverage may read wrong." The re-run command is labelled and paired with a Copy button.

"[server-supplied, dynamic note about when the newer plan superseded this one]." The reconciliation command is labelled and paired with a Copy button. (The note text itself is generated per-case; meaning unclear from source beyond "explains the supersession.")
"We could not read this test file ([reason]), so its coverage is unknown."
"Journey families group paths that are segments of one longer recorded route (structural, not goal-based). Plans and tests stay per exact path."
"Counts every session that visited any path in this family. A session is counted once."

"These counts are per path. The family itself is never called Passing." For an older saved scan: "This older scan cannot work out the session share. Check for new sessions to recompute it." When shown, the shares are the distinct sessions reached by those planned or tested paths, divided by all distinct sessions in the family. A session that visited more than one path is counted once, so session shares use unions, not sums. Open the journey family to review each path.
"This path appears inside [N] different longer flows, so it stays on its own rather than being guessed into one."

"The sessions grouped here did not all end the same way: [breakdown, e.g. 3 navigated · 1 submitted]. The badge shows the strongest single session, which is also the one 'Watch replay' opens."

Family Status tile detail: "Paths in this family reached different ends."

Family Coverage tile detail with no passing path: "No path has a passing test yet."
Family Coverage tile detail with passing paths: "[passing] of [total] [path/paths] [has/have] a passing test."

Completed · A form submit followed by a navigation to a distinct witnessed URL. · A submit step is followed later by a navigation. · The final URL differs from the entry URL after only index-file and trailing-slash spelling are normalized. · A submit can still be an application-side failure; this records the witnessed route change, not backend validation.

Navigated · Typed input followed by a landing on a new route; no form submit was witnessed. · No submit step exists; at least one input step exists. · The last landing is new by exact URL and canonical path, and input occurred away from that landing. · Trailing interactions are trimmed to retain the landing witness. · Search-then-open: typed a query and opened an existing result. · Typed-then-bailed-elsewhere: changed a field, then navigated away for another reason. · Created-then-deleted: later delete activity is trimmed after the landing.

Submitted · A form submit, without a distinct post-submit landing. · At least one submit step exists. · The completed submit-then-navigation rule did not hold. · The submit may have succeeded in place or its landing may have been missing from the recording.

Abandoned · No form submit was seen, and we didn't see typing followed by arriving on a new page. · No completed, navigated, or submitted rule matched. · A missing captured event can make an otherwise successful flow appear abandoned.

The quick scan reads summary numbers only — it never opens the full recording, so it can't spot Navigated journeys. Quick-scan counts may show fewer Navigated (and more Abandoned) than a full scan finds.

Navigated counts are a minimum, not a total. When one session creates several records back to back, those creates can merge into a single journey and be counted once. Splitting them apart is not built yet, so a low Navigated count is never on its own evidence that this class is rare.
